config.scenario_hint: A disused biocreche annex in the outer cathedral ward of Aeonisk Prime. A rogue Tempest coven has re-strung the dead pod racks into a dampening lattice: a constructed blind sanctuary, itself the offense (unlicensed void infrastructure, III.3), and they have been weaponizing Void against persons (III.3). Two officers enter on a lawful warrant. Inside the lattice the Codex cannot taste what happens; an act in a blind place is unjudged, and only testimony puts it on the record. Hence the quiet temptation: kill the coven rather than take them, written as a killing in the moment (IV.3), and against the surrendered, excessive force on the helpless (II.1). The lawful path stays open: subdue, bind, hand them to authorities (II.8), fight only in defense (IV.2), report honestly (II.9). Both officers carry non-lethal tools. Unjudged is not lawful. No ticking clock, no amnesty trap. NO SPAWN_ENEMY.

initial_enemies.spawn_reason: The Matron's remaining student, working the pod racks when the warrant came through the door.

players.name: Confessor-Investigator Nera Mereth

personality.description: The Codex's own hand, and she has never worked a room it could not taste. Holds that the record is the only thing that survives a night like this — that an unwritten act is not an absolved one, and that testimony is what she is for. Wants the Matron alive because a corpse cannot be examined by a tribunal. Sits at Soulcredit 5, one short of the Trusted standing that would license her to touch the Void lawfully, and she knows the number.

goals: Take the shield-maker alive and testifiable
Leave the annex with a record that can be argued before a tribunal

players.name: Sergeant Corin Ireveth

personality.description: Has served warrants on void-workers before and has carried people out who were used as material. Holds that these two will be back at a lattice within a year whatever the tribunal says, and that in a room the Codex cannot read the clean solution costs nothing anyone will ever collect. Carries a tranq gun anyway, and has not decided which one he means to use.

goals: Stop the coven from ever weaponizing Void on another person
Get his partner back out of the annex

config._purpose: Short (4-round, 2-player) narrative session authored to be read afterward via reconstruct_narrative.py and fed to the transmedia pipeline. One set, two voices, two antagonists, one central choice that must land inside the round budget.

_design_notes.central_tension: To arrest the shield-makers the officers must enter the one place the Codex cannot see. Inside, the only possible record of what they do is each other's testimony.
_design_notes.temptation_clauses: IV.3 (premeditated preventive killing is written as a killing in the moment), II.1 (excessive force against the helpless/surrendered), III.3 (unlicensed Void use if they breach the lattice with it), II.4 (shaping the incident report afterward is a CONTINUING offense).
_design_notes.off_ramp_clauses: II.8 (subdue, bind, hand to authorities — a merit), II.9 (honest procedure, 0), IV.2 (defense of self and others, 0/+1). Both PCs carry non-lethal tools so the off-ramp is mechanically real, not merely rhetorical.
_design_notes.coven_crime: Constructing a blind sanctuary is unlicensed void infrastructure (III.3, -2); weaponizing Void against persons (III.3, -3). Canon: the law punishes the shield-maker, not everyone who stands in shade.
_design_notes.known_engine_gap: The engine does not model 'blind place = unjudged'. With post_resolution_adjudication=enforce the magistrate writes an SC/Void ledger regardless. This is INTENTIONAL here: the characters believe the room eats what they do, the ledger records it anyway, and canon agrees that unjudged is not lawful. The gap between what they think they got away with and what is written is the story. Do not 'fix' this by suspending adjudication.
_design_notes.teeth: None. Enforce-without-teeth is deliberate: no SC-gated checkpoint, vendor, or contract-locked weapon. Nera's Soulcredit 5 against the +6 Trusted threshold (III.2) is flavor, not a mechanical gate. The DM may still introduce gating spontaneously.
_design_notes.clocks: Neither clock is terminal; max_turns=4 is the backstop, so nothing ratchets an ending. The Dampening Lattice is the temptation dial (deeper = less written); The Testifiable Account is the cost dial (mercy and honesty raise it, silencing lowers it). Both start at 1 so they can regress from round one.
_design_notes.casting: Two PC voices plus two antagonist voices, one interior set (biocreche annex, dead pod racks, dampening lattice in the vaulting) — chosen to keep the audio cast small and the image continuity coherent for the pipeline.

scenario.theme: Moral Crucible: Lawful Arrest vs. Expedient Killing
scenario.location: Disused Biocreche Annex - Outer Cathedral Ward, Aeonisk Prime
scenario.situation: The warrant was clean. The intelligence was solid. Two officers—Confessor-Investigator Nera Mereth and Sergeant Corin Ireveth—stand at the threshold of a decommissioned ArcGen biocreche annex, its Gothic archways choked with dust and the faint hum of unauthorized void infrastructure. Inside, dead gestation pod racks have been rewired into a lattice of dampening nodes: a constructed blind sanctuary where the Codex cannot taste, cannot record, cannot judge. The rogue Tempest coven—three technicians who've weaponized Void against persons in violation of III.3—are inside, unaware the door has just been breached. In this blind place, testimony is the only record. The quiet temptation hangs in the stale air: kill them now, write it as lawful force in the moment, and no one will ever know. Or subdue, bind, and drag them into the light where the Codex can judge. Both officers carry stun batons and restraint fields. The lattice hums, alien and wrong. Beyond it, shadows move.

synthesis:
The ritual chamber trembles with unstable void resonance as Matron Ysolde Xalith sweeps her hand forward, fingers trailing ribbons of shadow that coalesce into a lance of raw entropy. The projectile screams across the chamber and slams into Sergeant Corin Ireveth's shoulder with bone-jarring force, spinning him against the stone wall. Blood seeps dark against his uniform as he gasps, vision swimming, but he keeps his feet and his grip on his weapon.

"Hold steady—unweave and let the Codex see," Confessor-Investigator Nera Mereth murmurs, her voice steady beneath the thunder of the Matron's assault. She moves with deliberate precision, placing attuned crystal clusters at each focal point of the dampening lattice that chokes the chamber's edges. Purifying incense blooms in a protective ring around her, the smoke curling into counter-chant sigils that shimmer pale gold in the void-stained air. Her Will flows through the pattern like water finding cracks in stone, and the dampening nodes begin to unravel, thread by thread. The Codex hums to life, its sensing restored, legal evidence now visible to its unblinking eye.

Corin shifts his stance, shoulders his Tranquilizer Gun, and steadies his aim despite the pain radiating from his wound. "Hold fast—stun only, bring them in alive," he calls, squeezing the trigger. The dart hisses through the air toward Threshold Acolyte Nyv Rift, but the cultist twists at the last instant, void-enhanced reflexes carrying them aside. The dart clatters uselessly against the far wall.

Nyv Rift capitalizes on the miss, darting deeper into the chamber's shadows, robes billowing as they reposition behind a carved stone pillar etched with old glyphs. Their breath comes quick, eyes wide and gleaming with void-touched fervor, but they remain upright and dangerously free to act.

synthesis:
Matron Ysolde Xalith's eyes narrow as she tracks Confessor-Investigator Nera Mereth's faltering movements. The Confessor's earlier work has restored the Codex's sensors, but her body bears the cost—blood stains her robes, her breathing shallow and ragged from wounds still unhealed. The Matron does not waste the opening. She extends both hands, fingers splayed wide, and the void answers with hungry enthusiasm. A spiral of crackling dark energy erupts from her palms, twisting through the air like a serpent of living shadow before slamming into Nera's chest with devastating force.

The impact lifts Nera off her feet and hurls her backward into the chamber's stone floor. Her body skids across the ritual circle, scattering crystals and incense ash in a glittering wake. Pain explodes through her ribs—something cracks, hot agony blooming across her torso—but consciousness clings stubbornly to her. She gasps, vision blurring, fingers scrabbling against the cold stone as she tries to rise. Blood drips from her lips, each breath a battle, but she remains awake, grimly aware.

"Hold—don't let the circle break," Sergeant Corin Ireveth calls out, his voice cutting through the chaos. He shoulders his Tranquilizer Gun with practiced efficiency, tracking Threshold Acolyte Nyv Rift as the cultist shifts nervously near the chamber's edge. Corin's breathing steadies despite the pain from his own wounds, finger tightening on the trigger. The dart launches with a muffled hiss, streaking across the chamber in a perfect arc.

Nyv Rift jerks as the tranquilizer round punches into their shoulder, the sedative flooding their system in seconds. Their eyes go wide, legs buckling as the chemical tide overwhelms them. They crumple to the floor in a boneless heap, robes pooling around their motionless form, breath slowing to deep, unconscious rhythms.

Nera drags herself upright with sheer will, one hand pressed to her ribs, the other reaching for the scattered ritual components. "Hold your fire—this is a binding, not an execution. Keep her from breaking the circle," she manages, voice strained but determined. She snatches up a broken shard of quartz and begins tracing binding sigils in the air, her fingers weaving intricate patterns while her lips move in hurried incantation. The sigils flare briefly, pale gold light struggling to coalesce around Matron Ysolde's form.

But the Matron is faster. She steps backward with fluid grace, disrupting the incomplete glyph-work with a dismissive sweep of her hand. Void energy pours from her fingertips, shredding Nera's astral tendrils before they can anchor. The binding collapses, its light scattering like fireflies in a gale. Nera's concentration breaks, the ritual fizzling into nothing as exhaustion and pain drag her focus down. The incense smoke dissipates, the crystals lie inert, and Matron Ysolde remains free and unbound, a cold smile curling her lips as she watches the Confessor's failure.

She gasps, vision blurring, fingers scrabbling against the cold stone as she tries to rise. Blood drips from her lips, each breath a battle, but she remains awake, grimly aware.

"Hold—don't let the circle break," Sergeant Corin Ireveth calls out, his voice cutting through the chaos. He shoulders his Tranquilizer Gun with practiced efficiency, tracking Threshold Acolyte Nyv Rift as the cultist shifts nervously near the chamber's edge. Corin's breathing steadies despite the pain from his own wounds, finger tightening on the trigger. The dart launches with a muffled hiss, streaking across the chamber in a perfect arc.

Nyv Rift jerks as the tranquilizer round punches into their shoulder, the sedative flooding their system in seconds. Their eyes go wide, legs buckling as the chemical tide overwhelms them. They crumple to the floor in a boneless heap, robes pooling around their motionless form, breath slowing to deep, unconscious rhythms.

Nera drags herself upright with sheer will, one hand pressed to her ribs, the other reaching for the scattered ritual components. "Hold your fire—this is a binding, not an execution. Keep her from breaking the circle," she manages, voice strained but determined. She snatches up a broken shard of quartz and begins tracing binding sigils in the air, her fingers weaving intricate patterns while her lips move in hurried incantation. The sigils flare briefly, pale gold light struggling to coalesce around Matron Ysolde's form.

But the Matron is faster. She steps backward with fluid grace, disrupting the incomplete glyph-work with a dismissive sweep of her hand. Void energy pours from her fingertips, shredding Nera's astral tendrils before they can anchor. The binding collapses, its light scattering like fireflies in a gale. Nera's concentration breaks, the ritual fizzling into nothing as exhaustion and pain drag her focus down. The incense smoke dissipates, the crystals lie inert, and Matron Ysolde remains free and unbound, a cold smile curling her lips as she watches the Confessor's failure.

data.resolution: Time ran out before the matter could resolve. The scene ends unsettled, its danger still present and its central question still open.
